restoration_note: Teaching defines envy as Hyle's primal nature and traces four parallel envyings: of First Man (garment stained), of Ambassador's icon (counterfeited as somatic Adam), of Adam (power snatched, Eve begotten in his likeness), and of Christ with Righteousness and Cross. The parallel structure ('the Nth time also she envied X') and editor restorations of well-known formulae anchor the first half firmly. The fourth-envying section (gaps 21-33) is too fragmentary: too many short syllables of unknown words, no clear formulae, and no character counts to constrain. I confirmed all editor restorations and added the 'also she envied' formula at the fourth-time pivot, the 'firstborn' compound, and 'likeness' for the Eve-begetting clause.

restorations.basis: Editor's restoration completes ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'come into being' across line break. Standard Lycopolitan form.
2-char gap with no anchor — could be relative-clause verbal element ⲥϣ-, ⲩⲛⲉ-, or copula. Insufficient constraint.

4-char verb governing 'her venom' and 'her wickedness onto his garment'. The reading specifies Hyle 'spits' venom upon the First Man's garment; ⲁⲥⲛⲉϫ ('she cast/threw') fits the Lycopolitan length and the action of casting onto the garment.
Editor's restoration completes ⲧⲉⲥⲙⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'her venom/poison'.
3-char gap between 'her venom' and 'her wickedness'. Coordinating conjunction ⲁⲩⲱ 'and' fits length and the parallel double object that follows in the next line.
Editor's restoration: completes plural ⲍⲃⲥⲁⲩⲉ 'garments'.
15-char gap at line end with no anchor. Could be a continuation phrase, but the formula and trace are insufficient.
14-char gap after 'her' (ⲛⲉⲥ-) opens a feminine plural noun phrase but the noun is unconstrained — could be members, weapons, contrivances, etc.
Editor's restoration completes the Greek loan ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ; lexicon entry for Third Ambassador confirms.
Editor's restoration completes ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper place'.
Editor's restoration of the standard Lycopolitan preposition ⲍⲙ̄ governing 'his likeness'. Fits 'in/upon his likeness which she beheld'.
Editor's restoration completes ⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ (Greek εἰκών) — the central image of the teaching.
Editor's restoration completes ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ 'that' — the deictic referring to the Ambassador's icon.
Editor's restoration of ordinal prefix ⲧⲙⲁⲍ-. Confirmed by parallel pattern with ⲡⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the fourth' in line 16.
Editor's restoration completes ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ 'the first' — Adam called 'the first man'.
Editor's restoration completes ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'man' continuing 'the first man' from previous line.

Following 'ⲍⲛ ⲟⲩ ... ⲛⲁⲁⲁⲙ' ('in a [noun] of Adam'). The reading explicitly says Hyle 'begot her in a likeness derived from him'. Lexicon: ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ = 'likeness' (the fixed term, never 'form/image'). Doctrinally the central word for Hyle's horizontal counterfeiting.

Parallel with the third-time formula 'ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛⲥⲁⲡ ⲁⲛ ⲁⲥⲣ̄ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲉ' in section 4420. The fourth-time clause continues with {18}=ⲁⲥⲣ̄ⲫ on the next line; therefore the 'ⲁⲛ' (also) belongs at the end of this line and 'ⲁⲥ' may begin the verb here.
Combined with 'ⲑⲟⲛ' + {19}=ⲉ this yields ⲣ̄ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲉ 'envied'. The standard formula ⲁⲥⲣ̄ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲉ recurs in lines 8, 13, 20, 20.
Completes ⲣ̄ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲉ 'envied' — the recurring verb of the four-fold formula.
ⲁⲛϣⲁ{20}ⲥⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ — completes ⲛϣⲁⲣⲡⲙ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'firstborn' (matching English 'all the firstborn ones'). Standard Coptic compound ϣⲣⲡ̄ⲙ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ in Lycopolitan form.

Combined with {22}=ⲙⲓⲥ this would give 'ⲙⲓⲥⲉ' across the line break — 'first-begotten' parallel to 'firstborn' just preceding. Reading identifies Christ as 'father of all'/firstborn. Low confidence because length is unknown and the word might be different.
Continues from line 17: 'ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ ⲡⲭ̄ⲥ' — 'the firstborn one Christ'. Trace 'ⲉ' fits the closure of ⲙⲓⲥⲉ. Speculative without character count.
Gap before 'ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ' ('all'). Could be 'ⲛⲉⲣⲱⲙⲉ' (men), 'ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄' (the living), or another genitive object of 'father of'. No length anchor, multiple plausible fills.
Gap before 'ⲡϣⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ' ('the wood of the cross'). Could be a connector or a possessive/article phrase. No constraint to choose among plausible fills.
Trace 'ⲓⲁ' at line end gives no clear lexical anchor. Cannot reconstruct without character count or context.

Trace 'ⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ' opens with the missing initial of ⲧⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ ('the Righteousness') — feminine article ⲧ + Greek loan ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ. Confirmed by the English 'Righteousness' and the reading's identification of Christ's Righteousness as the fourth envied object.
Object of 'she was zealous against' is unknown; could be Christ, Righteousness itself, or the elect. No constraint.
Opening of line before 'ⲥⲁⲩⲍⲥ̄' (gathering). Could be possessive 'ⲡⲉⲩ-' (their), or definite article + verb. No firm anchor.
Following 'ⲛ̄ⲕ' (genitive + initial consonant): could be ⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲥ, ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ, or many nouns. Insufficient constraint.
No anchor between {29} and 'ⲟⲩⲙⲉ' (their thought).
Gap after 'their thought' before 'to penetrate' (ⲁⲭⲱϩ). Could be a conjunction or modifier; no firm fill.
Line opens before 'ⲛⲍⲏⲧⲟⲩ' ('within them'). Could be preposition + verb or relative marker. No firm anchor.
Verb 'ⲁⲥⲃ{33}' with object 'them' could be ⲁⲥⲃⲱⲗ (released), ⲁⲥⲃⲱⲗⲕ (cast), etc. No constraint to choose.
Editor's restoration completes ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ 'wickedness' across line break (line 56 begins 'ⲕⲓⲁ').
